result.question: Why did David’s men swear that he must never again go out with them to battle?

readings.answer: So that the lamp of Israel would not be extinguished
readings.support: so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished

readings.answer: Because he had needed rescue from a Philistine
readings.support: came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him

assessments.reason: It directly quotes the stated purpose clause: “so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished,” which matches the key.

The sequence “came to his aid… Then David’s men swore to him” reasonably implies they swore because he needed rescue, though the text explicitly gives their stated purpose as protecting the “lamp of Israel.”
